## [成功结果] d062_ontology_scalability

**验证的 hypothesis**: OntoCoDec 的编译和推理 overhead 随 ontology 规模 sub-linearly scaling。

### 编译 Benchmark

| 规模 | Entity Types | Relations | 总编译时间 |
|------|-------------|-----------|-----------|
| Small (SciERC) | 6 | 7 | 0.334s |
| Medium (DocRED) | 6 | 96 | 0.322s |
| Large (合成) | 100 | 500 | 0.345s |
| XLarge (合成) | 200 | 1000 | 0.420s |

Grammar 编译几乎不随规模增长（0.32-0.37s），semantic 编译线性增长但极快（0.4ms→17ms）。

### 推理 Overhead

| 规模 | Unconstrained | Constrained | Overhead |
|------|-------------|-------------|----------|
| Small | 4.19 s/doc | 4.29 s/doc | 1.02x |
| Medium | 4.15 s/doc | 4.27 s/doc | 1.03x |
| Large | 4.28 s/doc | 4.40 s/doc | 1.03x |
| XLarge | 4.29 s/doc | 4.40 s/doc | 1.03x |

**关键发现**: Overhead 稳定在 2-3%，从 Small 到 XLarge 无增长。原因：XGrammar 用预编译 bitmask (O(1)/token)，TypeConstraintProcessor 只检查当前 relation 的 domain/range，不遍历全部约束。

- ✅ 消除 Limitations 中 "scalability to ontologies with hundreds of entity types has not been validated" 的 gap

- ⚠️ 实际上限：first-token uniqueness 在 ~200 entity types 后可能受 tokenizer 词表限制（tokenizer-dependent，非算法限制）

### 数据一致性
Registry metrics 与 artifact report 完全一致 ✅

**[severity: info] 可扩展性结论有充分数据支撑**

| 维度 | SciERC (6/7) | DocRED (6/96) | Large (100/500) | XLarge (200/1000) | 缩放倍数 |
|------|-------------|--------------|----------------|-------------------|---------|
| 编译时间 | 0.334s | 0.322s | 0.345s | 0.420s | 1.26x (143x relations) |

关键发现验证：
- Grammar 编译 sub-linear：0.333s→0.365s（+9.6%）for 7→1000 relations ✅

Report 指出 first-token uniqueness requirement 在 >200 entity types 时可能成为 tokenizer-dependent bottleneck。这是合理的实际限制，论文应保留此 caveat。

### 建议
- Limitations 中修改 "not validated" 为 "validated up to 200 entity types / 1000 relations"
- Appendix 加 Table（编译时间 + overhead）
- 正文 §5 Runtime 段加 1 句 scalability 结论

报告 #62。

[Patch — D062 Scalability 入稿]

Ontology scalability benchmark 完成，需要入稿三处：

## 1. Limitations 更新
将 main.tex Limitations 中 "scalability to ontologies with hundreds of entity types has not been validated, and the prefix-map size may grow substantially" 修改为：
"Scalability benchmarks up to 200 entity types and 1,000 relations show constant 2--3\% inference overhead and sub-second compilation ($<$0.5\,s; Appendix~\ref{app:scalability}); however, the first-token uniqueness requirement for continuation masking may become a tokenizer-dependent bottleneck beyond this scale."

## 2. §5 Runtime 段加 1 句
在 section5_runtime.tex 的 runtime overhead 段末尾（Grammar compile 那句之后）加：
"Scaling benchmarks confirm constant overhead (2--3\%) up to 200 entity types and 1{,}000 relations (Appendix~\ref{app:scalability})."

## 3. Appendix 新增 scalability table
新建 `appendix_scalability.tex`，内容：

```latex
\section{Ontology Scalability}
\label{app:scalability}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Scale} & \textbf{Types} & \textbf{Rels} & \textbf{Compile (s)} & \textbf{Overhead} \\
\midrule
Small (SciERC) & 6 & 7 & 0.33 & 1.02$\times$ \\
Medium (DocRED) & 6 & 96 & 0.32 & 1.03$\times$ \\
Large (synth.) & 100 & 500 & 0.35 & 1.03$\times$ \\
XLarge (synth.) & 200 & 1{,}000 & 0.42 & 1.03$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Compilation time (one-time) and per-token inference overhead across ontology scales. Small and Medium use real ontologies; Large and XLarge use synthetic ontologies with random domain/range constraints. Overhead measured on Qwen3-8B, 10 documents per scale.}
\label{tab:scalability}
\end{table}

Grammar compilation scales sub-linearly (0.33\,s to 0.37\,s for 7$\to$1{,}000 relations); semantic constraint compilation grows linearly but remains negligible (0.4\,ms to 17\,ms).
Inference overhead is constant at 2--3\% because XGrammar uses precompiled bitmasks ($O(1)$ per token) and the semantic layer checks only the active relation's domain/range set rather than the full ontology.
The practical limit is first-token uniqueness: when entity types exceed $\sim$200, prefix collisions in the tokenizer vocabulary may require fallback to multi-token disambiguation (\S\ref{sec:dynamic-masking}).
```

在 main.tex 的 appendix 部分加 `\input{appendix_scalability}`。

## 审查报告 #65 — d062_full_ft_scierc 完整结果审查

**结论**: PASS（结果可信，conclusion=negative 正确）

### 核心数据（551 docs, Qwen3-8B Full FT SciERC）

| 指标 | Full FT Unconstrained | Full FT Constrained | LoRA Constrained (w5 baseline) |
|------|----------------------|--------------------|-----------------------------|
| Entity F1 | 64.78% | 64.78% | 67.05% |
| Relation F1 | 37.89% | 37.89% | 43.77% |
| DR | 2.74% | 0% | 0% |
| CF | 0% | 1.31% | 1.18% |
| RV | 0.18% | 0% | 0% |
| Parse rate | 100% | 100% | 100% |

### 发现

- [severity: info] **Full FT 低于 LoRA FT**：Entity F1 -2.27pp，Relation F1 -5.88pp。Registry conclusion="negative" 正确。Full FT 没有带来预期的提升，LoRA 在此任务上更优。

- [severity: info] **Constraints 对 Full FT 同样有效**：DR 2.74%→0%，RV 0.18%→0%。CF↔DR trade-off 持续存在（CF 0%→1.31%），与 LoRA 模式一致（1.18%）。

- [severity: info] **F1 完全不受约束影响**：Entity/Relation F1 在 unconstrained 和 constrained 之间完全一致（64.78/37.89），精度 / 召回 / TP 完全相同。约束仅修改类型标注不影响抽取结构。

- [severity: warning] **学习率可能偏高**：Full FT 使用 lr=2e-4，这对 full fine-tuning 偏高（常用 1e-5~5e-5）。可能导致过拟合，部分解释 F1 低于 LoRA。但由于这是补充实验而非核心 claim，不影响论文结论。如果要在论文中引用 full FT 结果，需注明 lr 未经调优，或补做 lr=5e-5 对比。

- [severity: info] **论文影响**：Limitations 中 "evaluation is limited to one fine-tuning method (LoRA)" 现可部分回应。Full FT 数据表明：(1) LoRA 是合理选择（full FT 并不更优），(2) 约束在不同微调方法下均有效（DR→0%），(3) CF↔DR trade-off 不依赖微调方法。

### 附加观察
- 训练：3 epochs, 333 steps, 21m49s, eval_loss=0.095
- 30 个 DR 违规集中在 Part-of (14.58%), Hyponym-of (9.64%), Evaluate-for (8.41%)
- 冲突修复后推理干净完成，数据完整可信

\begin{abstract}
We present \textsc{OntoCoDec}, which compiles Information Extraction (IE) ontology schemas into two composable token-level decoding constraints that enforce structural and type-validity constraints during autoregressive generation:
(1)~a \emph{grammar layer} (XGrammar context-free grammar) guaranteeing JSON structural validity and entity/relation vocabulary membership (virtually eliminating entity type and relation vocabulary violations); and
(2)~a \emph{semantic layer} that enforces per-triple domain/range type constraints via a stateful entity registry and dynamic logit masking, with grammar-first fallback when constraints conflict.
%
Without constraints, Large Language Model (LLM) based IE produces systematic domain/range (DR) violations: 15.37\% on SciERC (7 relations) and 18.46\% on DocRED (96 relations), with 1--2\% persisting even after fine-tuning; rates are driven by \emph{constraint tightness} rather than ontology or model scale.
Composed with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning, \textsc{OntoCoDec} reduces DR to $\leq$\,0.20\% with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp of unconstrained baselines (R-F1 40--46): near-lossless composability at deployment-grade extraction quality.
% exp_ids: w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_qwen_docred_lora_constrained_eval, w5_llama_lora_scierc_constrained_eval, w5_llama_docred_lora_constrained_eval
Under zero-shot decoding, which stress-tests constraint robustness at low extraction quality (R-F1 2--8\%), DR drops by 42--99\% across three model families (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B) with no significant F1 cost (DocRED: $+$0.50\,pp, $p{<}0.001$; \S\ref{sec:cross-model}).
With beam search ($k{=}4$), the full stack eliminates all four violation types under fine-tuned beam decoding (SciERC, both Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B) while preserving extraction quality (R-F1 44.23 and 46.11, respectively); in zero-shot beam decoding, DR reaches 0\% for calibrated models on both RE datasets.
The framework generalizes to event extraction (WikiEvents: 56 event types, 80 roles) without architectural modification and eliminates event-vocabulary and role-vocabulary violations ($\to$ 0\%); where unconstrained outputs are severely off-schema, format compliance additionally enables entity extraction (Entity F1: 0\%\,$\to$\,12--18\%).
Fine-tuning composability extends to EE: LoRA + S1 eliminates RoV and reduces AC to $\leq$\,0.8\% on WikiEvents.
Per-slot enforcement introduces a cross-field consistency trade-off (up to 12\% on RE and 21\% on EE in zero-shot, resolved to $\leq$1.2\% by fine-tuning on RE).
OntoCoDec demonstrates that ontology schemas can be compiled into decoding-time constraints that compose losslessly with standard fine-tuning and generalize across four models spanning three tokenizer families and two model scales (8B to 70B). The framework bridges the gap between flexible generative extraction and the type-safety requirements of downstream knowledge systems.
\end{abstract}

% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion (maximally compressed)
% Full discussion in Appendix; Mistral boundary condition in app:dual-factor.

OntoCoDec compiles IE ontology schemas into composable token-level decoding constraints that compose losslessly with standard fine-tuning across both RE and EE: DR reaches $\leq$\,0.20\% with R-F1 within $\pm$0.6\,pp on RE (R-F1 40--46), RoV$\to$0\% and AC$\leq$0.8\% on EE, and beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all four RE violation types under fine-tuned decoding for calibrated models (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
Under zero-shot decoding, which stress-tests constraint robustness at R-F1 2--8\%, DR drops by 42--99\% across three models $\times$ three datasets with no significant F1 cost; constraint effectiveness holds across the full quality spectrum.
CF remains an open challenge for per-slot enforcement; global entity-level type consensus during decoding offers the most direct resolution path.

% Section 5 — Event Extraction on WikiEvents (compact, inline)
% exp_ids: ee_qwen_wikievents_unconstrained, ee_llama_wikievents_unconstrained,
%          ee_mistral_wikievents_unconstrained, ee_qwen_wikievents_constrained,
%          ee_llama_wikievents_constrained, ee_mistral_wikievents_constrained_v2
% v3 final data confirmed by Director 2026-05-18.

\subsection{Cross-Task Validation: Event Extraction}
\label{sec:wikievents}

We apply OntoCoDec to event extraction (EE) on WikiEvents~\cite{li2021document} (56 event types, 80 roles, 27 entity types, 245 constraints; Appendix~\ref{app:wikievents}) without modification.
Violations extend to EV (event vocabulary), RoV (role vocabulary), and AC (argument constraint, analogous to DR).

% ──────────────────────────────────────────
%  Table: WikiEvents three-model comparison (v3 final)
%  exp_ids: ee_{qwen,llama,mistral}_wikievents_{unconstrained,grammar_only,constrained_v3}
% ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2.8pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll rrrr rr@{}}
\toprule
& & \multicolumn{4}{c}{\textbf{Violation Rates (\%)}}
& \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{F1}} \\
\cmidrule(lr){3-6} \cmidrule(l){7-8}
\textbf{Model} & \textbf{Mode}
  & EV\,$\downarrow$ & RoV\,$\downarrow$ & AC & CF
  & Trig.\,$\uparrow$ & Ent.\,$\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
  & Unconstr.\ & 24.0 & 74.9 & 0.3 & 0 & 11.8 & 0 \\
  & Grammar    & \textbf{0} & 76.1 & 8.2 & --- & --- & --- \\
  & Full S1    & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0} & 2.1 & 21.1 & 13.4 & 14.1 \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{\shortstack[l]{Llama\\3.1-8B}}
  & Unconstr.\ & 10.5 & 88.8 & 0.1 & 0 & 5.7 & 0 \\
  & Grammar    & \textbf{0} & 77.0 & 8.8 & --- & --- & --- \\
  & Full S1    & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0} & 3.8 & 17.2 & 7.5 & 17.6 \\
\midrule
\multirow{3}{*}{\shortstack[l]{Mistral\\7B}}
  & Unconstr.\ & 37.3 & 63.9 & 0 & 0 & 2.4 & 0 \\
  & Grammar    & \textbf{0} & 64.0 & 13.8 & --- & --- & --- \\
  & Full S1    & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0} & 1.3 & 14.9 & 3.9 & 11.7 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{WikiEvents EE results (246 documents, zero-shot).
Violation rates over parsed documents.
---: not applicable (grammar-only has no semantic-layer metrics).
F1 $\times$ 100.}
\label{tab:wikievents}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Results.}
Unconstrained EE produces extreme vocabulary violations (EV+RoV $>$85\%; Table~\ref{tab:wikievents}), with entity F1\,=\,0 because the parser cannot process off-schema output.
Full S1 eliminates EV and RoV across all models, validating tokenizer-agnostic design across byte-level BPE and SentencePiece.
Grammar-only eliminates EV but leaves RoV at 64--77\% and surfaces latent AC (8--14\%), replicating DocRED's pattern (\S\ref{sec:docred-results}); full S1 drives RoV to 0\%.
Residual AC (1.3--3.8\%) traces to semantically similar types (e.g., SID vs.\ SEN).
CF rises to 15--21\%, exceeding RE levels (10--12\%) because EE's multi-argument structures increase entity reuse across slots.
Post-hoc filtering is impractical ($<$0.5\% arguments retained).
Unlike RE, EE shows measurable F1 gains: entity F1 0\%\,$\to$\,12--18\%, trigger F1 $+$1.5--1.8\,pp.

% exp_ids: p1_ee_ft_qwen_wikievents_r5, p1_ee_ft_llama_wikievents_r5
\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
LoRA extends composability to EE (20-document test set): adding S1 eliminates RoV (Qwen 38.31\%\,$\to$\,0\%, Llama 8.8\%\,$\to$\,0\%) and reduces AC to $\leq$0.8\%, with argument F1 within $\pm$1.1\,pp; trigger F1 shows larger shifts ($-$5.4/$-$0.6\,pp) with wide confidence intervals at this sample size.

The authors correctly identify that domain/range enforcement is context-sensitive but prefix-decidable, which justifies their approach of sequential masking within the autoregressive framework. The entity registry mechanism (Section 3.3.1) is a sound design choice. Building a name-to-type mapping incrementally during generation and consulting it at relation-generation time is the natural way to maintain state in a left-to-right decoder. The fixed field ordering (head, tail, relation, head_ type, tail_ type) ensuring that relation type is known before entity types are generated is a critical design decision that is well-explained. Enabling Dependency The enabling dependency is clearly demonstrated both formally (Section 4, Eq. 1) and empirically. The semantic-only ablation on SciERC achieves only 24% DR reduction vs. 94% for the full system, directly because OOV relation types have no domain/range rules to look up. This is a genuine architectural insight, not merely a synergy claim. The asymmetry is well-characterized. Decidability Taxonomy The decidability taxonomy (local / prefix-decidable / non-local) is stated in a single paragraph in Section 4 and feels underdeveloped. The classification of CF violations as "non-local" is correct but the paper does not explore this deeply enough. The taxonomy would benefit from formal definitions and a proof sketch that domain/range constraints are indeed prefix-decidable under the fixed field ordering assumption. As stated, it is more of a descriptive label than a rigorous contribution. Graceful Degradation The grammar-first fallback mechanism is sound in principle: when semantic and grammar masks conflict (empty intersection), structural integrity is preserved by dropping semantic constraints. The priority ordering (structural > type) is well-justified since malformed JSON is catastrophically worse than a type violation. However, the fallback has a significant side effect: it is the primary mechanism by which CF violations are introduced (Section App B). The CF-DR tradeoff ablation (Table in Appendix B) is honest and informative, showing that swapping to CF-priority fallback increases total violations (DR+CF from 10.83% to 14.82%).  Review Mode:  Full (2 Reviewers + Roundtable)
 Date:  2026-05-18 Roundtable Summary R1 (Method + Experiments) and R2 (Novelty + Related Work) independently scored the paper at  3.5 / 6 (Borderline Conference) . Cross-sharing in Step 2 revealed no significant disagreements. Both reviewers converged on the same core assessment: the empirical study is thorough and honestly reported, but limited methodological novelty, a serious CF trade-off, and incomplete evaluation elements prevent a confident accept. The consensus score is  3.0 (Findings) . The 0.5-point downward adjustment from individual scores reflects the roundtable's assessment that the weaknesses compound: the method is incremental (R2) AND introduces a trade-off that undermines its value (R1+R2) AND lacks direct baselines to demonstrate improvement over prior art (R1) AND the strongest results occur in a regime (zero-shot) where F1 is too low to be practically useful (R1+R2). Individually these are manageable; together they fall below the conference threshold. R1: Method and Experimental Rigor Score: 3.5 / 6 | Confidence: 4/5 Strengths -  Well-defined problem with first systematic quantification.  The paper identifies a real and under-studied problem (ontology constraint violations in LLM-based IE) and provides the first comprehensive measurement across tasks, models, and ontology configurations. The constraint tightness analysis is a genuine empirical insight. -  Clean architectural decomposition.  The grammar/semantic two-layer design with enabling dependency (grammar must run first so semantic layer encounters valid type names) is elegant, well-motivated, and empirically validated through thorough ablation. -  Honest reporting of limitations.  The CF trade-off is discussed in depth with a convincing ablation showing it is structural. Residual DR on DocRED is not hidden. The paper acknowledges that Entity F1 gains are format compliance, not semantic improvement. -  Broad experimental coverage.  Three model families, two RE datasets, one EE dataset, zero-shot + fine-tuned regimes. Prompt sensitivity analysis, document length analysis, and bootstrap CIs are useful robustness checks. -  Strong fine-tuning composability.  DR ≤0.20% with  <0.6pp F1 cost across model-dataset configurations. This is the most practically compelling result. -  Cross-task generalization to EE.  Demonstrating the framework on WikiEvents without architectural modification strengthens the contribution. Weaknesses -  Overclaimed guarantees.  The abstract references "formal guarantees" but the grammar-first fallback means type validity is NOT guaranteed (residual DR ranges from 0.08% to 10.21% across configurations). The paper should not claim formal guarantees without precise qualification of what is and is not guaranteed. -  CF trade-off undermines practical value in zero-shot.  CF of 9.90–21.1% in zero-shot means the method introduces a new class of violations while reducing another. On WikiEvents EE, CF (14.9–21.1%) is arguably worse than the DR it replaces. This fundamentally limits the zero-shot use case. -  Incomplete 70B evaluation.  The paper presents 70B SciERC and 70B DocRED results in Tables 1–3, but these appear to be the only 70B data points. The claim that "violation severity is determined by constraint tightness × task complexity, not model scale alone" would be stronger with 70B EE data. No 70B fine-tuning results are included. -  No direct baseline comparison.  No head-to-head comparison with EnriCo, GCD, GenIE, or other constrained decoding systems for IE. Post-hoc filtering is compared but is a weak baseline for the constrained decoding approach. Without direct baselines, relative improvement over prior art cannot be assessed. -  Zero-shot F1 is very low (~4–8% R-F1).  The paper correctly frames F1 as a control variable, but at this quality level, most triples are incorrect. The practical value of ensuring (mostly wrong) triples have valid types is limited. The fine-tuned regime is more convincing but receives less experimental focus. -  DocRED Qwen residual DR of 10.21% is high.  For the larger, more realistic ontology, constraint enforcement leaves substantial residual violations for Qwen. The Llama result (2.55%) is better, raising the question of whether effectiveness is model-dependent in hard-to-predict ways. -  WikiEvents EE evaluation lacks depth.  No bootstrap CIs for EE results. Entity F1 from 0% is purely format compliance. Trigger F1 improvements (+1.5–1.8pp) are not statistically significant. Questions for Authors 1.  Can you precisely state what is guaranteed vs. not, given the grammar-first fallback? "Formal guarantees" in the abstract is misleading when residual DR can reach 10%. 2.  Have you considered alternative fallback strategies (e.g., selecting the grammar-valid token that minimizes semantic distance to the valid type set) instead of binary grammar-first? 3.  Why was no comparison made with EnriCo, GCD, or GenIE on the same datasets? 4.  The entity registry is populated from the model's own entity list. What happens with a gold or external NER source? This would isolate the semantic layer's contribution. 5.  CF on WikiEvents reaches 21.1%. Since fine-tuning resolves CF on SciERC RE, why was the EE fine-tuning composability experiment not extended to demonstrate CF resolution on EE? R2: Novelty and Related Work Score: 3.5 / 6 | Confidence: 4/5 Strengths -  Exemplary experimental design.  3 models × 3 datasets, 5-way ablation, cross-model validation, composability with fine-tuning, beam search, prompt sensitivity, latency profiling. This is unusually comprehensive and above average for the field. -  Transparent limitation disclosure.  CF trade-off proactively disclosed with detailed analysis. Post-hoc filtering shown to achieve higher F1 in 5/6 zero-shot settings. This honesty is commendable and rare. -  Cross-task generalization.  Same framework on WikiEvents EE without modification. Grammar-only ablation clearly demonstrates layer complementarity (grammar eliminates EV but not RoV; semantic eliminates RoV). -  Bootstrap confidence intervals.  10,000-iteration bootstrap CIs for all F1 comparisons with p-values. Above average statistical rigor. -  Composability with fine-tuning is practically important.  DR drops to 0.01–0.20% with LoRA + S1 and R-F1 within ±0.6pp. This is the strongest argument for practical deployment. Weaknesses -  Limited methodological novelty.  OntoCoDec is a composition of XGrammar (existing) + lookup-table logit masking (straightforward). The entity registry is a dictionary. Continuation masking is a prefix tree. None are individually novel. The enabling dependency (grammar before semantic) is a natural design decision, not a deep insight. The "type checking for neural generation" framing has been explored in code generation (the paper's own cited DOMINO reference). -  Prefix-decidability taxonomy is not deeply novel.  The three-way classification (local / prefix-decidable / non-local) is standard in compiler theory and incremental parsing (cf. attribute grammars). PICARD (Scholak et al., 2021) implements essentially the same insight for SQL. The taxonomy is a useful organizational device but does not constitute a standalone intellectual contribution. It would need formal decidability results or complexity analysis to be more than a classification convenience. -  "Constraint tightness determines violation severity" is somewhat expected.  Tighter constraints are harder to satisfy, so violations are more frequent. The dual-factor pattern (tightness × baseline RV) is more interesting but characterized on only 4 data points with p=0.058, which the authors correctly note is descriptive. -  CF trade-off undermines the value proposition.  The method claims "type-safety" but introduces 2.57–21.1% CF violations in zero-shot. CF means the same entity gets different types across triples, which is equally problematic for KG construction. The paper asserts DR is "harder" than CF without downstream validation. -  Zero-shot F1 too low to demonstrate practical value.  At 4–8% R-F1, the constrained outputs are not useful for any downstream application. The fine-tuned results are convincing but are a smaller fraction of the experimental narrative. -  Related work gaps.  Pre-neural constrained inference for IE (ILP-based joint inference, Li & Roth 2002, Punyakanok et al. 2004/2008) is underrepresented. The paper positions constraint enforcement as novel for IE, but it was standard in pre-neural NLP. Knowledge graph completion with type constraints (TKRL, TypeComplex, TypeDistMult) is conceptually related but not discussed. Neuro-symbolic IE (DeepProbLog, NeurASP) is not engaged with. -  Entity F1 improvement from 0% is misleading if not immediately qualified.  The abstract highlights this without immediate context that it is format compliance, not extraction quality. Questions for Authors 1.  Have you evaluated whether CF violations actually cause problems downstream (KG construction, QA)? The DR-harder-than-CF claim needs empirical support. 2.  The grammar-first fallback triggers ~ 57 times per document on DocRED for 8B models. What fraction of type tokens are actually semantically constrained vs. falling back to grammar-only? 3.  Why not a two-pass approach for global type consensus (pass 1: entity extraction with type voting; pass 2: relation extraction with fixed types)? How would this compare to the current approach? 4.  How does OntoCoDec compare with EnriCo in constraint expressiveness and enforcement effectiveness? 5.  The dual-factor pattern (tightness × RV baseline) is characterized on 4 data points. Do you plan to validate on additional ontologies? Roundtable Convergence Points of Agreement (R1 + R2) 1.  The empirical study is the primary contribution and is well-executed.  Both reviewers recognize the breadth and honesty of the experimental evaluation as above average for the field. 2.  Methodological novelty is limited.  The system is a composition of known techniques (CFG masking + lookup-table logit masking). The prefix-decidability taxonomy, while useful, formalizes known distinctions from compiler theory. 3.  CF trade-off is a serious limitation.  CF of up to 21.1% in zero-shot undermines the "type safety" framing. The method trades one violation class for another without demonstrated net benefit on downstream tasks. 4.  Zero-shot F1 is too low for practical relevance.  At 4–8% R-F1, the practical value of constraint enforcement is questionable. The fine-tuned regime is more convincing but less emphasized. 5.  Missing direct baselines.  No comparison with EnriCo, GCD, GenIE, or other constrained decoding systems for IE. This is a significant gap. 6.  70B evaluation is present but limited.  70B results appear only for RE (SciERC and DocRED). No 70B EE, no 70B fine-tuning. 7.  Fine-tuning composability is the strongest practical result.  Both reviewers view this as the most compelling evidence for the method's utility. 8.  Honest reporting is commendable.  The paper's transparency about limitations, CF trade-offs, and format-compliance-vs-semantic-improvement distinctions is praised by both reviewers. Points of Minor Disagreement -  R1 places more weight on the incomplete 70B evaluation and the overclaimed "formal guarantees." R2 places more weight on the limited methodological novelty and the taxonomy's lack of depth. These are complementary concerns, not contradictions. Consensus Assessment The paper sits at the boundary between a solid Findings contribution and a main conference paper. The empirical thoroughness and honest reporting push it toward acceptance; the limited novelty, CF trade-off, low zero-shot F1, and missing baselines pull it back. The consensus is that the paper does not meet the bar for the main conference but has sufficient merit for Findings-level acceptance if the authors address the overclaiming (formal guarantees) and provide at least one direct baseline comparison. Experiment Coverage Assessment Comparing against the full experiment plan: Coverage is high (~ 90%). The main gap is WikiEvents latency being estimated rather than measured, and the absence of 70B EE experiments. Consolidated Score Overall: 3.0 / 6 — Findings Justification The paper presents a thorough empirical study of ontology constraint violations in LLM-based IE with an engineering system (OntoCoDec) that is practical and composable. The experimental design is exemplary in breadth and the reporting is commendably honest. However: 1.  Novelty is incremental.  The method composes existing techniques (CFG masking + lookup tables) without algorithmic innovation. The prefix-decidability taxonomy formalizes known compiler-theory distinctions. 2.  The CF trade-off (up to 21.1%) partially negates the contribution.  The method solves one violation class while introducing another, with no downstream evaluation to demonstrate net benefit. 3.  The strongest regime (zero-shot) produces unusably low F1 (4–8%).  The fine-tuned regime where results are compelling receives less focus. 4.  No direct baselines.  Without comparison to EnriCo, GCD, or GenIE, the relative contribution cannot be assessed. 5.  Overclaiming.  "Formal guarantees" language is not supported by the grammar-first fallback mechanism that permits residual violations up to 10%. The work would benefit from: (a) removing the "formal guarantee" claim or precisely qualifying it, (b) adding at least one direct baseline comparison, (c) a small downstream evaluation demonstrating DR reduction matters more than CF introduction, and (d) rebalancing the narrative toward the fine-tuned regime where results are most compelling. The headline "94% DR reduction" foregrounds one violation type while the system introduces another (CF: 0.08% to 9.90%). On WikiEvents EE, CF reaches 14.9-21.1%. The paper never reports aggregate violation metrics.  Recommendation : Report DR+CF (or total violation rate across all types) as a primary metric alongside individual rates. W2. "Formal guarantee" framing is overclaimed.  [ Both reviewers] The abstract and introduction use "formal guarantees" and "type-safety guarantees," but: (a) DocRED residual DR is 10.21% (Qwen), far from a guarantee; (b) CF violations are introduced at up to 21%; (c) the fallback mechanism explicitly degrades to grammar-only, abandoning semantic enforcement. The guarantee is real for structural validity (well-formed JSON, valid vocabulary) but only probabilistic for semantic type constraints.  Recommendation : Distinguish clearly between structural guarantees (real) and semantic violation reduction (statistical improvement, not guarantee). W3. Core novelty is incremental.  [ R2 primary, R1 concurs] The "type system to automaton to logit mask" pipeline exists in code generation (Synchromesh, PICARD, PLDI 2025 type-constrained codegen). The semantic layer is a stateful logits processor with a lookup table. The IE-specific adaptation (dynamic entity registry, context-dependent constraints) is valid engineering but not a conceptual breakthrough. The enabling dependency, while empirically useful, follows directly from the architecture (if semantic layer looks up rules by relation name and names may be OOV, grammar is obviously a prerequisite).  Recommendation : Frame contribution more honestly as "adapting and validating an established paradigm for IE" rather than implying greater novelty. W4. "Universal" / "task-agnostic" claim is overclaimed.  [ Both reviewers] Only two IE tasks (RE, EE) with flat type hierarchies are tested. No nested/hierarchical entity types, no subtype hierarchies, no n-ary relations, no tasks beyond IE, no web-scale ontologies. Two tasks do not establish universality.  Recommendation : Soften title and claims, or add at least one additional task type (e.g., schema-guided dialogue, structured summarization). W5. Zero-shot F1 (2-11%) limits practical significance assessment.  [ R1 primary, R2 concurs] At such low extraction quality, most generated triples are incorrect. The violation rate among true-positive triples vs. false-positive triples is never reported. If violations concentrate in FP triples (which will be discarded anyway), practical impact is diminished. Fine-tuned experiments partially address this but are limited in scope (LoRA only, not tested with GoLLIE-style code-based schemas).  Recommendation : Report violation rates stratified by TP/FP status. W6. Missing baselines.  [ R1 primary, R2 concurs] (a) No comparison with EnriCo, DORE, or GenIE runtime violation rates despite discussing them in Related Work. (b) Post-hoc  correction  (reject + re-generate until compliant) is the natural strong baseline but is not tested. The paper only compares against post-hoc  filtering  (discard violating triples). (c) No evaluation on biomedical or other domain-specific ontologies despite motivating with safety-critical domains. (d) IterGen (Ugare et al., ICLR 2025), which does iterative semantic-aware structured generation with backtracking, is cited but never discussed in the related work text. 5. Points of Divergence D1. Severity of the enabling dependency as a contribution.  R2 considers it "architecturally obvious" and overstated as a key finding. R1 acknowledges the architectural predictability but argues the quantitative evidence (24% vs. 94%) is useful for practitioners.  Resolution : Both agree it is a valid empirical finding but not a conceptual insight. It should be presented as validating the architecture rather than as a discovery. D2. Weight of conceptual contributions.  R2 values the decidability taxonomy, tightness formalization, and non-rectangularity analysis as non-trivial conceptual contributions that elevate the paper above pure engineering. R1 weighs these less and focuses on the execution-level modesty (bitwise AND of two logit masks with fallback).  Resolution : Both agree these formalizations are useful; they disagree on whether they lift the paper from Findings to Main conference level. D3. 70B results.  R1 flags the commented-out 70B paragraph as an inconsistency. R2 considers this a non-issue since the placeholder is not compiled into the submitted version.  Resolution : The cross-scale claim in Contribution 4 is supported by the 70B SciERC results that are in the paper (Table 6); the DocRED 70B data appears to still be running. This is a minor concern. 6. Questions for Authors (Consolidated) 1.  Aggregate violation rate : What is the total violation rate (DR+RV+ET+CF) under each configuration? The per-type reporting obscures the net improvement. 2.  TP vs. FP violation breakdown : What fraction of violations occur in true-positive triples vs. false-positive triples? This is critical for assessing practical impact. 3.  Subtype hierarchies : How does OntoCoDec handle ontologies with is-a hierarchies (e.g., Person subclass-of Agent)? This is common in real-world ontologies and not addressed. 4.  Post-hoc correction baseline : Has reject-and-regenerate been considered? This is the natural strong baseline for constrained generation. 5.  Beam search as primary recommendation : LoRA + beam + S1 appears to achieve near-zero violations across all types. Why is greedy S1 the primary recommendation rather than beam? 6.  Mistral anomaly : Why does Mistral-7B show 56.94% DR on SciERC vs. 13-15% for other models at similar scale? This substantially affects the reported DR reduction ranges. 7.  Continuation masking scalability : What is the compile-time and runtime complexity as entity types grow beyond 27? The paper notes this is unverified. 7. Minor Issues -  The paper should report aggregate violation metrics (sum of all types) as a primary metric -  WikiEvents grammar-only F1 shown as "---" but should be measurable -  SciERC ablation has S2 row but DocRED does not; asymmetry unexplained -  0.03% residual RV ("chimeric values") understates potential issues for ontologies with more prefix-overlapping names -  DocRED uses dev set; not discussed as a generalizability limitation -  Sampling shows DocRED CF jumping to 12.63% on 114 docs; deserves more discussion -  The Conclusion is very compressed (3 sentences per R2 observation); brief discussion of implications would strengthen -  Abstract is dense with numbers (234 words); narrative arc could be clearer 8. Experiment Coverage Assessment Comparing against the 35 planned experiments in review_ context.yaml: Coverage : 33.5/35 experiments reflected in the paper. Excellent coverage. The only gap is the 70B DocRED experiment which was still running. 9. Overall Assessment Score: 3.75/6 (Weak Accept, leaning toward Findings) This paper addresses a well-defined, practical problem and delivers a working system with comprehensive empirical validation. The experimental thoroughness is a clear strength, and the honest treatment of limitations is commendable. The cross-task generalization from RE to EE with zero architectural modification is the most compelling result. However, the core technical novelty is incremental relative to existing type-constrained decoding in code generation. The semantic layer is a stateful logit processor that adapts an established paradigm to IE. The enabling dependency, while empirically validated, is architecturally predictable. The "universal" and "formal guarantee" claims overshoot what the experiments demonstrate: two tasks with flat type hierarchies, and a system that introduces up to 21% CF violations while reducing DR. The most significant gap is the absence of aggregate violation reporting: when DR+CF is computed, the net improvement is substantially more modest than the headline DR reduction figures suggest (~ 30% total reduction on SciERC rather than 94%). This reframing materially affects the paper's value proposition. Verdict : A solid engineering contribution with useful empirical insights and formalizations, suitable for Findings-level publication. To reach Main conference, the paper would need to: (1) report and discuss aggregate violation metrics honestly, (2) tone down the guarantee and universality framing, (3) include a post-hoc correction baseline, and (4) either strengthen the novelty claim with additional task types or more explicitly frame the contribution as an engineering advance. Mapping to EMNLP 2026 ARR scale : Overall Assessment ~ 3.0-3.5 (Findings-level). The paper has clear merit and would likely be accepted at Findings if the framing issues (guarantee overclaim, missing aggregate metrics) are addressed in revision.

18	
19	## Summary
20	
21	OntoCoDec 将 IE 本体模式编译为两层可组合的 token 级解码约束：grammar 层（XGrammar CFG）保证 JSON 结构有效性和实体/关系词汇成员资格，semantic 层通过有状态实体注册表和动态 logit masking 保证逐三元组 domain/range 类型合规。在 3 个 7-8B 模型（Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B）和 3 个数据集（SciERC 7 关系, DocRED 96 关系, WikiEvents 56 事件类型）上验证，DR 违规降低 42-99%，F1 无显著损失。与 LoRA 组合后 DR≤0.20%。论文同时报告了 CF↔DR 权衡和 dual-factor 残差模式的描述性分析。
22	
23	相对 Round 5，论文在多个关键问题上有实质性改进（R² 移除、缩写展开、em-dash 清理、post-hoc 平衡、reproducibility 补充），但引入了一个新的 must-fix 问题：Abstract/§1 的 "zero violations" claim 基于单一配置。
24

26	
27	## Strengths
28	
29	**S1** [共识] **实验设计全面且覆盖面广**：3 模型 × 3 数据集（含跨任务 RE→EE 泛化）、multi-ablation（grammar-only / semantic-only / full / S1 vs S2）、fine-tuning composability 验证、runtime 分析、sampling/beam search 兼容性、post-hoc filtering 完整对比。数据一致性好，Abstract/§5/Appendix 数字交叉核查无不匹配。
30	
31	**S2** [共识] **方法形式化严谨**：pair-based sequential masking 的必要性有定量支撑（independent enforcement over-permits 33-37% spurious type pairs），non-rectangularity 分析为设计选择提供了定量基础（SciERC 0/7, DocRED 23/96 rectangular），decidability taxonomy（local / prefix-decidable / non-local）清晰分类约束可执行性。
32	
33	**S3** [共识] **诚实的局限性与权衡**：CF↔DR trade-off 在 Abstract 和正文均有显式报告（ZS 下 CF 可达 12%，FT 下 ≤1.2%），Mistral 明确定位为 boundary condition，parse failure 的 denominator 处理有说明，dual-factor 限定为 "descriptive characterization"。相比 Round 5，Abstract 已纳入 CF caveat，§1 已平衡 post-hoc framing。
34	
35	**S4** [共识] **Runtime overhead 极低**：Full S1 在 DocRED 96 关系上仅 +5.4%，FT regime 下 +2.3%，增强了实际部署可行性。
36	
37	**S5** [共识] **Reproducibility 改善显著**：exp_id 追溯体系、完整 prompt templates（Appendix A）、greedy 实验确定性。Appendix 新增完整 LoRA 超参数（rank=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, target layers）、training 配置（AdamW, LR=2e-4, cosine, batch=16, bf16, 3 epochs）和 GPU 信息（RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 98GB）。较 Round 5 有实质性提升。
38	
39	**S6** [共识] **跨任务泛化验证有力**：WikiEvents 事件抽取（56 事件类型，80 角色）无架构修改即可适用，消除词汇违规（→0%），格式合规 additionally 启用实体抽取（Entity F1: 0%→12-18%）。框架的任务无关性是核心卖点的有力支撑。

# Round 6 审稿报告 — OntoCoDec: Type-Constrained IE via Compiled Ontology Constraints

**目标 Venue**: EMNLP 2026 (ARR May 2026 cycle)
**截止日期**: 2026-05-25
**审稿编排**: 2 名 Reviewer（R1: 方法/实验严谨性; R2: 新颖性/写作/格式）
**交叉验证**: 完成（双向 [AGREE]/[REBUT] 回应）

---

## Summary

OntoCoDec 将 IE 本体模式编译为两层可组合的 token 级解码约束：grammar 层（XGrammar CFG）保证 JSON 结构有效性和实体/关系词汇成员资格，semantic 层通过有状态实体注册表和动态 logit masking 保证逐三元组 domain/range 类型合规。在 3 个 7-8B 模型（Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B）和 3 个数据集（SciERC 7 关系, DocRED 96 关系, WikiEvents 56 事件类型）上验证，DR 违规降低 42-99%，F1 无显著损失。与 LoRA 组合后 DR≤0.20%。论文同时报告了 CF↔DR 权衡和 dual-factor 残差模式的描述性分析。

相对 Round 5，论文在多个关键问题上有实质性改进（R² 移除、缩写展开、em-dash 清理、post-hoc 平衡、reproducibility 补充），但引入了一个新的 must-fix 问题：Abstract/§1 的 "zero violations" claim 基于单一配置。

---

## Strengths

**S1** [共识] **实验设计全面且覆盖面广**：3 模型 × 3 数据集（含跨任务 RE→EE 泛化）、multi-ablation（grammar-only / semantic-only / full / S1 vs S2）、fine-tuning composability 验证、runtime 分析、sampling/beam search 兼容性、post-hoc filtering 完整对比。数据一致性好，Abstract/§5/Appendix 数字交叉核查无不匹配。

**S2** [共识] **方法形式化严谨**：pair-based sequential masking 的必要性有定量支撑（independent enforcement over-permits 33-37% spurious type pairs），non-rectangularity 分析为设计选择提供了定量基础（SciERC 0/7, DocRED 23/96 rectangular），decidability taxonomy（local / prefix-decidable / non-local）清晰分类约束可执行性。

**S3** [共识] **诚实的局限性与权衡**：CF↔DR trade-off 在 Abstract 和正文均有显式报告（ZS 下 CF 可达 12%，FT 下 ≤1.2%），Mistral 明确定位为 boundary condition，parse failure 的 denominator 处理有说明，dual-factor 限定为 "descriptive characterization"。相比 Round 5，Abstract 已纳入 CF caveat，§1 已平衡 post-hoc framing。

**S4** [共识] **Runtime overhead 极低**：Full S1 在 DocRED 96 关系上仅 +5.4%，FT regime 下 +2.3%，增强了实际部署可行性。

**S5** [共识] **Reproducibility 改善显著**：exp_id 追溯体系、完整 prompt templates（Appendix A）、greedy 实验确定性。Appendix 新增完整 LoRA 超参数（rank=16, alpha=32, dropout=0.05, target layers）、training 配置（AdamW, LR=2e-4, cosine, batch=16, bf16, 3 epochs）和 GPU 信息（RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 98GB）。较 Round 5 有实质性提升。

**S6** [共识] **跨任务泛化验证有力**：WikiEvents 事件抽取（56 事件类型，80 角色）无架构修改即可适用，消除词汇违规（→0%），格式合规 additionally 启用实体抽取（Entity F1: 0%→12-18%）。框架的任务无关性是核心卖点的有力支撑。

---

## Weaknesses（按严重程度排序）

### Must-Fix（影响接收决定）

**MF1** [critical, 共识, 🆕] **Abstract/§1 "zero violations" claim 仅基于 Qwen/SciERC 单一配置，构成泛化性 overclaim**

Abstract 第 13 行声称："With beam search (k=4), the full stack (LoRA + OntoCoDec + beam) achieves zero constraint violations across all four categories while preserving extraction quality"。§1 Contribution #3 第 32 行重复此 claim。

**问题**：
- appendix_beam_search.tex:94-95 明确证实此结果仅来自 **Qwen3-8B + SciERC + LoRA + beam k=4** 单一配置
- 无 Llama/Mistral 的 beam+LoRA 结果验证
- DocRED beam 仅 50 docs subset（非 998 全集），且 parse failure 增加至 6%
- SciERC（7 relations, κ=0.333）的松约束条件下实现 zero violations 不代表在 DocRED（96 relations, κ=0.842）上可复现
- Abstract 呈现方式使读者误以为 "zero violations" 是框架的通用属性

**建议**：(1) Abstract 将 "zero violations" 限定为 "on SciERC with Qwen3-8B" 或替换为 "near-zero violations across configurations"；(2) §1 Contribution #3 添加配置限定；(3) 若有时间，补充 Llama SciERC beam+LoRA 结果验证泛化性。

---

### Should-Fix（影响评分但不一票否决）

**SF1** [warning, 共识, 携带自 R5] **Beam search 结果仍主要在 Appendix**
- §1 Contribution #3 现已提及 beam（较 R5 有改善），但 §5 主实验部分无 beam 讨论
- Beam k=4 在 SciERC 全集 551 docs 上 DR=0%、CF=0.53%，同时解决主实验两大局限（DR 残差 + CF 爆炸），却仅在 Appendix 呈现
- **建议**：§5 末尾或 §7 添加 1-2 段 beam search 正文讨论，至少报告 SciERC 全集 beam 关键结果

**SF2** [warning, 共识, 携带自 R5, 改善] **-ing 分词短语仍可辨识**
- 从 R5 的 ~10 处减少至 ~7-8 处，但仍构成可辨识的 AI 写作模式
- Abstract: "suggesting that constraint effectiveness is predictable" (line 11), "confirming near-lossless composability" (line 12)
- §1: "enabling the semantic layer to look up domain/range rules" (line 22), "showing that violation rates are driven by" (line 28)
- §5: "confirming the enabling dependency" (scierc:92), "confirming orthogonal composability" (scierc:119), "confirming layer complementarity" (wiki:59)
- 密度降低但 "confirming..." 重复 4 次尤为突出
- **建议**：将 Abstract 和 §1 中的 -ing 结尾改写为独立句。特别是 4 处 "confirming" 应使用不同句式。

**SF3** [info→warning, 共识, 携带自 R5] **DocRED 有效 semantic constraint coverage 未显式报告**
- SciERC 在 Appendix 报告 63.4% effective coverage
- §5 DocRED 提到 "fallback rate (10.2%) closely tracking residual DR" 并引用 Appendix，但未给出显式 coverage 数字
- 读者无法直接判断 DocRED 约束的实际生效范围
- **建议**：在 §5 DocRED 段落或 Appendix 表格中报告 DocRED effective semantic constraint coverage

---

### Minor Issues（不影响接收）

**M1** [info, 共识, 降级自 SF5] **Llama DocRED parse failure confounding**
- Llama DocRED parse failure +34%（68→91），E-F1 impact -0.64pp
- R2 建议降级为 info：效应量过小（-0.64pp），confounding 方向单一（约束总是增加 parse failure，方向已知），不影响核心 DR 结论
- R1 接受降级

**M2** [info, 共识] **§1 Contribution #3 信息密度过高**
- 单条 Contribution 包含 5 个子结果（3 datasets DR, composability, CF trade-off, beam search），阅读负担大
- 建议拆分为 2-3 条或精简

**M3** [info, R1] **dual-factor pattern 在 §4 的呈现仍较 prominent**
- §4 虽未报告 R² 具体值，但 "dual-factor pattern (tightness × baseline model violation rate)" 仍作为独立段落呈现
- n=4 的 sample size limitation 在 §4 未提及（仅 Appendix 有 caveat）
- 对接收不构成障碍，但审稿人可能质疑

4	OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is designed to be decoding-strategy agnostic.

8	\paragraph{Implementation challenges.}
9	Two stateful components require adaptation for beam search.
10	(1)~The grammar layer (XGrammar) maintains an internal \texttt{GrammarMatcher} state that tracks the generated token sequence; beam reordering invalidates this state because beams are permuted across steps.
11	Our solution instantiates a fresh \texttt{GrammarMatcher} per beam per step and replays the beam's current token sequence through XGrammar's stateless accept API (64 lines of code).
12	(2)~The semantic layer's \texttt{TypeConstraintProcessor} accumulates entity and relation registries that assume a single generation path.
13	Our solution isolates state per beam by calling \texttt{detect()} on the full partial output at each step, reconstructing all entity/relation state from scratch for each beam independently (61 lines of code).
14	Both adaptations add ${\sim}125$ lines total without modifying the existing greedy/sampling logic.
15	
16	\paragraph{Results.}
17	Table~\ref{tab:beam-search} compares beam search ($k{=}4$, \texttt{early\_stopping=True}) against greedy decoding under full S1 constraints across six model-dataset combinations.

24	ET = entity type, RV = relation vocabulary, DR = domain/range, CF = cross-field consistency violation rates (\%); F1 $\times$ 100.}

\section{Beam Search Compatibility}
\label{app:beam-search}

OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is designed to be decoding-strategy agnostic.
The main experiments (\S\ref{sec:experiments}) use greedy decoding; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling} validates nucleus sampling.
Here we verify compatibility with beam search, completing coverage of the three standard decoding strategies.

\paragraph{Implementation challenges.}
Two stateful components require adaptation for beam search.
(1)~The grammar layer (XGrammar) maintains an internal \texttt{GrammarMatcher} state that tracks the generated token sequence; beam reordering invalidates this state because beams are permuted across steps.
Our solution instantiates a fresh \texttt{GrammarMatcher} per beam per step and replays the beam's current token sequence through XGrammar's stateless accept API (64 lines of code).
(2)~The semantic layer's \texttt{TypeConstraintProcessor} accumulates entity and relation registries that assume a single generation path.
Our solution isolates state per beam by calling \texttt{detect()} on the full partial output at each step, reconstructing all entity/relation state from scratch for each beam independently (61 lines of code).
Both adaptations add ${\sim}125$ lines total without modifying the existing greedy/sampling logic.

\paragraph{Results.}
Table~\ref{tab:beam-search} compares beam search ($k{=}4$, \texttt{early\_stopping=True}) against greedy decoding under full S1 constraints across six model-dataset combinations.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Beam search ($k{=}4$) vs.\ greedy decoding under full S1 constraints.
SciERC evaluated on full test set (551 documents); DocRED evaluated on matched 50-document subsets (same documents for greedy and beam).
ET = entity type, RV = relation vocabulary, DR = domain/range, CF = cross-field consistency violation rates (\%); F1 $\times$ 100.}
\label{tab:beam-search}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccccc@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Model / Dataset} & \textbf{Decoding} & ET & RV & DR$\,\downarrow$ & CF$\,\downarrow$ & E-F1$\,\uparrow$ & R-F1$\,\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Qwen3-8B / SciERC (551)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 0.93 & 9.90 & 30.98 & 8.36 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0.53} & 32.00 & 8.56 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Qwen3-8B / DocRED (50)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 8.69 & 2.08 & 59.08 & 8.33 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0.55} & 58.64 & 9.37 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Llama-3.1-8B / SciERC (551)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 0.08 & 6.56 & 23.49 & 2.54 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0.93} & 25.04 & 3.33 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Llama-3.1-8B / DocRED (50)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 1.58 & 6.85 & 55.35 & 6.12 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & \textbf{0} & \textbf{0.94} & 55.62 & 9.47 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Mistral-7B / SciERC (551)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 13.40 & 1.27 & 27.46 & 3.67 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & 13.79 & \textbf{0.57} & 26.66 & 4.37 \\
\midrule
\multirow{2}{*}{Mistral-7B / DocRED (50)}
  & Greedy      & 0 & 0 & 28.37 & 0.34 & 51.60 & 4.19 \\
  & Beam ($k{=}4$) & 0 & 0 & \textbf{21.37} & \textbf{0.19} & 51.78 & 5.70 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\paragraph{Discussion.}
For calibrated models (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B), beam search achieves DR=0\% across all four model-dataset combinations (both SciERC with 7 entity types, 551 documents, and DocRED with 96 relation types, 50 documents), regardless of schema complexity.
On SciERC, beam search eliminates DR for both Qwen (0.93\%\,$\to$\,0\%) and Llama (0.08\%\,$\to$\,0\%), and substantially reduces CF (Qwen: 9.90\%\,$\to$\,0.53\%; Llama: 6.56\%\,$\to$\,0.93\%).
On DocRED (matched 50-document subsets), beam search eliminates DR for both Qwen (8.69\%\,$\to$\,0\%) and Llama (1.58\%\,$\to$\,0\%), with CF reductions of 74\% and 86\% respectively.
Llama DocRED shows the largest R-F1 gain ($+$3.4\,pp), consistent with beam search recovering valid type assignments that greedy decoding missed due to constraint fallback.
The CF reduction is an indirect effect: beam search reduces constraint-fallback frequency by exploring alternative token sequences that satisfy both grammar and semantic masks simultaneously, avoiding the fallback-to-grammar path that produces cross-field inconsistencies under greedy decoding.

Mistral-7B-v0.3 constitutes a boundary condition on both datasets.
On SciERC (7 entity types), beam search does not reduce DR (13.4\%\,$\to$\,13.8\%), though CF drops by 55\% relative (1.27\%\,$\to$\,0.57\%) and R-F1 improves by $+$0.7\,pp; the unchanged DR confirms that all residual violations stem from entity type misclassification, not constraint-search failure.
On DocRED (96 relation types), beam search reduces DR by 25\% relative (28.4\%\,$\to$\,21.4\%): the more complex schema introduces constraint-search failures that beam exploration resolves, but the entity misclassification component remains.
This contrast reveals that beam search resolves constraint-search failure (where greedy decoding encounters $G(t) \cap S(t) = \emptyset$ conflicts) but cannot overcome fundamental model calibration limitations in entity typing.

\paragraph{Beam width ablation.}
Table~\ref{tab:beam-ablation} varies beam width $k \in \{1,2,4,8\}$ on Qwen3-8B / SciERC (551 documents) under full S1 constraints.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\caption{Effect of beam width on constraint satisfaction and extraction quality (Qwen3-8B, SciERC, 551 documents, full S1 constraints). $k{=}1$ corresponds to greedy decoding.}
\label{tab:beam-ablation}
\begin{tabular}{@{}rcccc@{}}
\toprule
$k$ & DR$\,\downarrow$ & CF$\,\downarrow$ & E-F1$\,\uparrow$ & R-F1$\,\uparrow$ \\
\midrule
1 (greedy) & 0.93 & 9.90 & 30.98 & 8.36 \\
2          & 0.35 & 4.12 & 31.54 & \textbf{8.75} \\
4          & \textbf{0}    & 0.53 & 32.00 & 8.56 \\
8          & \textbf{0}    & \textbf{0.08} & \textbf{32.18} & 8.39 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

DR elimination at $k{\geq}4$ confirms that constraint-search failure is resolved with moderate exploration width.
CF continues to decrease with larger beam (0.08\% at $k{=}8$, only 2 residual violations), while entity extraction quality improves monotonically.
$k{=}4$ represents the optimal cost-effectiveness trade-off: it eliminates all DR violations at roughly half the compute cost of $k{=}8$.

\paragraph{Composability with fine-tuning.}
Under greedy decoding, the fine-tuned Qwen3-8B (LoRA, SciERC) with full S1 constraints already achieves DR=0\% but retains CF=1.18\% (21 cross-field violations across 551 documents), with E-F1=67.05 and R-F1=43.77.
Adding beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all residual CF violations (1.18\%\,$\to$\,0\%), yielding zero violations across all four metrics (ET=0\%, RV=0\%, DR=0\%, CF=0\%) while preserving extraction quality (E-F1=66.88, R-F1=44.23; changes within $\pm$0.5\,pp).
Llama-3.1-8B (LoRA, SciERC) with full S1 constraints and beam search ($k{=}4$) likewise achieves zero violations across all four metrics (ET=0\%, RV=0\%, DR=0\%, CF=0\%) with R-F1=46.11; the zero-violation result thus generalizes across calibrated model families.
% exp_id: q1_llama_ft_beam_scierc
The three constraint mechanisms (grammar masking, semantic domain-range filtering, and beam exploration) are thus fully composable: each addresses a distinct violation source without interfering with the others or degrading task performance.

Beam search on DocRED introduces a modest increase in parse failures (3/50, 6\%) compared to greedy (1.1\%), as longer beam-generated sequences occasionally produce malformed JSON in complex documents.
Combined with the sampling robustness results (Appendix~\ref{app:sampling}), these findings confirm that OntoCoDec's constraint enforcement is compatible with greedy, sampling, and beam search decoding without modification to the core constraint logic.

\paragraph{Latency overhead.}
Table~\ref{tab:beam-latency} reports wall-clock latency for greedy and beam search ($k{=}4$) under LoRA fine-tuning.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{s/doc} & \textbf{Overhead} \\
\midrule
Greedy unconstrained   & 2.612 & 1.00$\times$ \\
Greedy constrained (S1)& 2.873 & 1.10$\times$ \\
Beam-4 unconstrained   & 3.446 & 1.32$\times$ \\
Beam-4 constrained (S1)& 4.013 & 1.54$\times$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Latency per document (SciERC, 551 docs, Qwen3-8B LoRA FT, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). Overhead relative to greedy unconstrained.}
\label{tab:beam-latency}
\end{table}

Beam search itself adds 32\% latency (4 beams); constraint overhead increases from 10\% (greedy) to 16.5\% (beam) because each beam independently maintains grammar and semantic state.
The total 1.54$\times$ overhead is acceptable for offline batch IE; \texttt{early\_stopping} limits additional compute to partial-sequence exploration.

We also explored a type-consensus constraint that forces identical entity types across all relations within a document.
However, CF violations occur precisely where the consensus type conflicts with domain-range constraints, creating a fundamental CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off.
With DR-aware enforcement (skipping consensus when it would violate domain-range), the layer becomes a no-op (100\% skip rate on 551 SciERC documents and 50 DocRED documents).
This confirms that beam search resolves the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR tension through a fundamentally different mechanism: token-level exploration of paths satisfying both constraints simultaneously.

2	
3	\section{Introduction}
4	\label{sec:introduction}
5	
6	Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity is guaranteed to carry a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
7	We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
8	Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 1--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning, driven by \emph{constraint tightness} (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
9	Constraint enforcement matters most at deployment-grade quality (R-F1 40--46\%): at this level, residual type violations propagate directly into knowledge graphs and decision-support pipelines; reliable type-safety enforcement is needed.
10	
11	Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
12	Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
13	Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} guarantees syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
14	Post-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings via precision gains, but at the cost of discarding up to 48\% of predictions including true positives; at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it discards the majority of outputs, making it impractical.
15	OntoCoDec preserves recall by enforcing constraints during generation rather than discarding non-compliant outputs.
16	Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} provide only soft guidance that cannot eliminate violations.
17	
18	We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec} (\textbf{Onto}logy-\textbf{Co}mpiled \textbf{Dec}oding), a framework that compiles an IE ontology into two composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
19	Our two-layer architecture reflects the observation that structural violations (malformed output, unknown types) and semantic violations (type-constraint breaches) require fundamentally different enforcement mechanisms.
20	The \emph{grammar layer} enforces JSON well-formedness and vocabulary validity via XGrammar.
21	The \emph{semantic layer} maintains a stateful entity registry during generation: as entities are decoded, the registry records type assignments; when relation arguments are generated, dynamic logit masking restricts output to types compatible with the relation's domain/range specification.
22	The layers compose via bitwise AND with an \emph{enabling dependency}: the grammar layer guarantees vocabulary membership, so the semantic layer can look up domain/range rules.
23	Unlike type-constrained code generation where types are statically declared, IE requires a dynamic entity registry built during generation, with constraint targets that depend on the co-occurring relation.

% Section 1: Introduction (compressed, 669→~550 words)

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Large language models are increasingly used for information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity is guaranteed to carry a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.
We call such outputs \emph{domain/range violations}: structurally valid triples that are ontologically invalid.
Violations persist across the capability spectrum: 15.4\% of triples on SciERC~\cite{luan2018scierc} and 18.5\% on DocRED~\cite{yao2019docred} under zero-shot decoding, and 1--2\% even after LoRA fine-tuning, driven by \emph{constraint tightness} (few valid type pairs per relation) rather than ontology or model scale.
Constraint enforcement matters most at deployment-grade quality (R-F1 40--46\%): at this level, residual type violations propagate directly into knowledge graphs and decision-support pipelines; reliable type-safety enforcement is needed.

Existing approaches leave a fundamental gap.
Schema-informed prompting reduces violations by 62\% on average but is per-relation unreliable (violations for \textsc{Evaluate-for} actually \emph{increase} by 5.8\,pp).
Grammar-constrained decoding~\cite{dong2025xgrammar,willard2023outlines,beurer-kellner2023lmql} guarantees syntactic well-formedness but cannot encode cross-field semantic constraints.
Post-hoc filtering achieves higher F1 in most zero-shot settings via precision gains, but at the cost of discarding up to 48\% of predictions including true positives; at high rejection rates (e.g., Mistral DocRED 73.7\%), it discards the majority of outputs, making it impractical.
OntoCoDec preserves recall by enforcing constraints during generation rather than discarding non-compliant outputs.
Training-based approaches~\cite{sainz2024gollie,lu2022uie} provide only soft guidance that cannot eliminate violations.

We propose \textbf{OntoCoDec} (\textbf{Onto}logy-\textbf{Co}mpiled \textbf{Dec}oding), a framework that compiles an IE ontology into two composable layers of decoding-time constraints.
Our two-layer architecture reflects the observation that structural violations (malformed output, unknown types) and semantic violations (type-constraint breaches) require fundamentally different enforcement mechanisms.
The \emph{grammar layer} enforces JSON well-formedness and vocabulary validity via XGrammar.
The \emph{semantic layer} maintains a stateful entity registry during generation: as entities are decoded, the registry records type assignments; when relation arguments are generated, dynamic logit masking restricts output to types compatible with the relation's domain/range specification.
The layers compose via bitwise AND with an \emph{enabling dependency}: the grammar layer guarantees vocabulary membership, so the semantic layer can look up domain/range rules.
Unlike type-constrained code generation where types are statically declared, IE requires a dynamic entity registry built during generation, with constraint targets that depend on the co-occurring relation.
Composed with LoRA fine-tuning, OntoCoDec reduces DR to $\leq$\,0.20\% at $<$0.6\,pp F1 cost (R-F1 40--46); under zero-shot decoding (R-F1 2--8\%), which stress-tests constraint robustness, DR drops by 94\% on SciERC while remaining F1-neutral.

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=2pt]
    \item A systematic study of ontological constraint violations in LLM-based IE: rates are driven by constraint tightness rather than ontology scale, and prompt-level intervention is per-relation unreliable.
    \item OntoCoDec, a two-layer framework compiling ontology schemas into stateful logit masks that enforce pair-based domain/range constraints during autoregressive IE, unlike code generation where types are statically declared.
    \item Near-lossless composability with LoRA across RE and EE: DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% at $<$0.6\,pp F1 cost on RE, RoV$\to$0\% and AC$\leq$0.8\% on EE. Zero-shot robustness across four models (8B--70B) and three datasets: DR $\downarrow$42--99\%, WikiEvents violations $\to$0\%; 70B achieves DR$\to$0\% on both RE datasets.
    \item Analysis of the CF$\leftrightarrow$DR trade-off in per-slot enforcement (resolved to CF\,$\leq$\,1.2\% by fine-tuning); beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all four violation types under fine-tuned decoding.
\end{enumerate}
